title: The secret promised
theme: Death promises to declare the secret, eternal Brahman, and how the self fares when it meets death.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «हन्तेदानीं», now then; Raṅgarāmānuja: spoken to himself, in wonder, «हन्त इति स्वगतम्, आश्चर्ये»

words.role: introduces the second object of pravakṣyāmi

words.context: Śaṅkara and Madhva: death; Raṅgarāmānuja: release, «आत्मा मरणम् - मोक्षं प्राप्य»

words.role: address: Naciketas, by his family name

sandhi.rule: e becomes ay before a vowel, P. 6.1.78 (एचोऽयवायावः), and the y is dropped, P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य), leaving the vowels apart.
A final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः).

sandhi_exceptions.note: prāpya ātmā stands unjoined at the pāda boundary in AS and the other witnesses; Madhva’s text joins it (prāpyātmā) and lacks ca (corrections.json). Unjoined, the third pāda keeps eight syllables.

morphology.note: The simple future of pra-√vac, ‘declare’: Death promises the teaching.
A patronymic, ‘descendant of Gotama’; Naciketas’ father is called Gautama at 1.1.10, and Death so addresses the son.

translation.literal: Come now, I shall declare to you this secret, eternal Brahman, and how the self fares, having reached death, O Gautama.
translation.readable: Now I will tell you this hidden, ancient Brahman, Gautama, and what becomes of the self when it meets death.

anvaya: हन्त गौतम ते इदम् गुह्यम् सनातनम् ब्रह्म प्रवक्ष्यामि । आत्मा मरणम् प्राप्य यथा च भवति [तत् च प्रवक्ष्यामि] ।
syntax: One verb, pravakṣyāmi, with two objects: the noun phrase idaṃ guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam and the clause introduced by yathā ca, ‘and how …’. The vocative gautama closes the verse.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: death, and what becomes of the self that does not know, which goes on in saṃsāra, «अविज्ञानाच्च यस्य मरणं प्राप्य यथा च आत्मा भवति यथा आत्मा संसरति तथा शृणु». Raṅgarāmānuja: release, «आत्मा मरणम् - मोक्षं प्राप्य», and what form the released self has. Madhva: death, and how the individual self fares, taught so as to show its difference from the Lord.
An encouraging ‘come now’ addressed to Naciketas (Śaṅkara), or Death’s own exclamation of wonder (Raṅgarāmānuja).

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 17 and 16 syllables: the first pāda has nine because te idam stands in hiatus (ta idaṃ); the second half-line has sixteen only with prāpya ātmā unjoined.

beginner: Death now promises Naciketas two things. He will explain the hidden, ancient Brahman, and he will explain what happens to a person, the self, when it meets death. This returns to the boy’s third question from the beginning of the story, about a man who has died. The commentators hear the promise differently. Śaṅkara says the second part concerns the person who has not understood: such a one goes on into new lives, as the next verse says. Raṅgarāmānuja reads ‘death’ here as release, so Death is promising to say what the freed self is like. Madhva says the point of the promise is to show that the individual self is different from the Lord.
analogy: Like a teacher who, after many lessons, says: now I will tell you the thing all of this was for.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Death promises to declare the secret, eternal Brahman, and how the self fares after reaching death.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: the knowing and the not knowing
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: He will tell the secret Brahman by whose knowledge all saṃsāra ceases, «यद्विज्ञानात्सर्वसंसारोपरमो भवति», and how the self that does not know fares after death, going on in saṃsāra, «यथा आत्मा संसरति तथा शृणु हे गौतम».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: For him maraṇa here is release, «आत्मा मरणम् - मोक्षं प्राप्य, यथा यत्प्रकारविशिष्टो भवति»: Death will tell the qualified pupil, free of passion, how the released self is, «मुमुक्षवे रागाद्यनुपहताय उपदेशयोग्याय तुभ्यं वक्ष्यामि इत्यर्थः».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: His comment on these words is filed in madhva.json under 2.1.2–3 (see the flags): he will tell the secret Brahman, and how the individual self fares after death, to make known the difference between the individual and the Lord, «इदं गुह्यं ब्रह्म प्रवक्ष्यामि । यथा मरणं प्राप्य जीवो भवति तच्च प्रवक्ष्यामि जीवेश्वरभेदज्ञापनाय».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: All agree that Death promises two things: Brahman, and the self’s state after death. They disagree on which self and which ‘death’: the self that does not know and so is reborn (Śaṅkara), the released self (Raṅgarāmānuja), or the individual self as distinct from the Lord (Madhva).

advaita.text: Knowledge of Brahman ends saṃsāra; without it the self goes on after death, «यद्विज्ञानात्सर्वसंसारोपरमो भवति».

visistadvaita.text: maraṇa is release, and Death promises to teach the form of the released self, «आत्मा मरणम् - मोक्षं प्राप्य».

dvaita.text: The teaching of the self’s state after death is given to show the difference of the individual from the Lord, «जीवेश्वरभेदज्ञापनाय».

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara and Madhva take maraṇa as death; Raṅgarāmānuja as release. Śaṅkara reads the second promise of the ignorant self’s rebirth; Madhva of the individual self as distinct from the Lord.

parallels.note: Naciketas’ third boon asked about the doubt concerning a man who has died; Death now promises to answer it.

contemporary.text: The teacher’s promise to speak plainly about death comes only after long preparation. Questions about death are often met either with silence or with quick answers; the dialogue suggests a third way, earned and careful. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Why do you think Death waits so long before speaking of death?
reflect.deeper: How does reading maraṇa as ‘release’ change the meaning of the next verses?
reflect.practice: Write down one question about life and death you would want to ask a wise teacher, and keep it.

flags.note: Madhva’s text lacks ca (yathā maraṇaṃ prāpya) and joins prāpyātmā (corrections.json).

madhva.json files Madhva’s comment on 2.2.6–2.2.8 (it glosses इदं गुह्यं ब्रह्म प्रवक्ष्यामि, the going to wombs and the one awake among the sleeping) under 2.1.2 and 2.1.3, where the source prints it; under 2.2.6–2.2.9 it files his comment on 2.2.9 (अग्निर्यथैको). It is cited here as madhva:2.1.2.
